[[Image:Gaura lindheimeri at Comox and Jervis, Vancouver.jpg|thumb|''Oenothera lindheimeri'' 'Siskiyou Pink']]

'''''Oenothera lindheimeri''''',<ref>[https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=835999 ITIS Standard Report Page: ''Oenothera lindheimeri''] . accessed 8.1.2013</ref><ref>Updated for ITIS by the Flora of North America Expertise Network, in connection with an update for USDA PLANTS (2007-2010)</ref> commonly known as '''Lindheimer's beeblossom''', '''white gaura''', '''pink gaura''', '''Lindheimer's clockweed''', and '''Indian feather''', is a species of ''[[Oenothera]]''.  Several of its common names derive from the genus ''[[Gaura]]'', in which this species was formerly placed.

The [[perennial plant]] is native to southern [[Louisiana]] and [[Texas]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 10 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=usda>USDA Plants Profile: [https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=GALI2 ''Gaura lindheimeri'']</ref>  The [[specific name (botany)|specific epithet]] is after [[Ferdinand Jacob Lindheimer]], a German-American botanist who extensively studied the plants of [[Texas]] for [[Harvard University]] professor [[Asa Gray]]. It is somewhat commonly grown as an ornamental plant in North America.

==Description==
''Oenothera lindheimeri'' is a [[perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]] growing to {{convert|50|to(-)|150|cm|round=5|sp=us}} tall, with densely clustered branched stems growing from an underground [[rhizome]]. The [[leaf|leaves]] are finely hairy, lanceolate, {{convert|1|to(-)|9|cm|frac=2|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|1|to(-)|13|mm|frac=16|abbr=on}} broad, with a coarsely toothed margin.

The [[flower]]s are produced on a {{convert|10|to(-)|80|cm||adj=mid|-long|round=5|sp=us}} [[inflorescence]]; they are pink or white, {{convert|2|to(-)|3|cm|frac=4|abbr=on}} in diameter, with four petals {{convert|10|to(-)|15|mm|frac=8|abbr=on}} long and long hairlike [[stamen]]s, and are produced from the beginning of spring until the first frost.<ref name=munz>Munz, P. A. (1938). Studies in Onagraceae XI. A Revision of the Genus Gaura. ''Bull. Torrey Bot. Club'' 65: 105-122, 211-228.</ref><ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Oenothera lindheimeri'' is an [[ornamental plant]]. It is used in either garden beds or pots. It grows best in full sun and can survive lengthy periods of [[drought]].

Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected for varying flower color, from nearly pure white in 'Whirling Butterflies' to darker pink in 'Cherry Brandy' and 'Siskiyou Pink'. In some cultivars, the petals are white at dawn then turn pink before falling off at dusk.

Although a perennial rated USDA Zone 6-9 for hardiness it may not overwinter reliably, and is often treated as an annual. In colder climates a heavy winter mulch is necessary.<ref>[http://www.perennials.com/plants/gaura-lindheimeri.html Perennials.com]</ref>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Oenethera lindheimeri''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/386413/Oenothera-lindheimeri-(G)/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=18 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 39 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 27 February 2018}}</ref>

==Etymology==

''Oenothera'': [[Etymology]] is uncertain, but it is believed to be derived from the [[Greek language|Greek]] phrase οίνος θήρα (''oinos thera'') meaning "wine seeker".<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NJ6PyhVuecwC&q=Oenothera |title=The Names of Plants |first=D. |last=Gledhill |edition=4 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-86645-3 |year=2008 |page=278}}</ref>

''Gaura'': Derived from Greek {{lang|grc|γαῦρος}} ''(gaûros)'' meaning "superb". Named in reference to the stature and floral display of some species in this genus.<ref>Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  [https://books.google.com/books?id=NJ6PyhVuecwC&q=Gaura p. 175.]</ref>

''Lindheimeri'': The plant is named for [[German Americans|German-American]] botanist [[Ferdinand Lindheimer]] (1801–79).<ref>Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  [https://books.google.com/books?id=NJ6PyhVuecwC&q=Lindheimeri p. 238.]</ref>
